data.title: Oakmark Global Select Fund Q3 2026 Commentary
data.description:
Third Quarter 2026

  • The Fund (Investor Class) outperformed the benchmark, the MSCI World Index, for the quarter.
  • At the sector level, the largest contributors to performance were health care and information technology, while consumer discretionary and industrials were the largest detractors.
  • Geographically, the top three regional allocations are 61.1% in the U.S., 22.2% in Europe ex U.K. and 9.5% in the U.K. For the quarter, the U.S., Germany and China were the largest contributors to performance. Denmark, France and the Netherlands were the largest detractors from performance. Emerging markets accounted for 3.0% of the portfolio.
  • During the quarter, a handful of large companies continued to dominate U.S. market returns, and international markets contended with currency, economic, and geopolitical uncertainty. However, these factors have also created attractive opportunities in select areas of the market. By remaining focused on well-managed businesses selling at discounts to our estimate of intrinsic value, we believe patient investors are well-positioned to benefit as the gap between price and value narrows over time.

Highlights

Top contributors

  • IQVIA Holdings (IQV)
  • Salesforce (CRM)
  • Becton Dickinson (BDX)

Top detractors

  • DSV (DSDVF)
  • Molina Healthcare (MOH)
  • LVMH (LVMHF)

New purchases

  • Amrize (AMRZ)
  • LVMH
  • Willis Towers Watson (WTW)

Final sales

  • BMW (BMWKY)
  • ConocoPhillips (COP)

Top contributor

IQVIA was a contributor during the quarter. Shares of the U.S.-headquartered healthcare data, analytics, and clinical research services provider rose after the company reported strong Q2 results, highlighted by double-digit bookings growth and accelerating organic revenue growth reflecting an improving demand environment and higher win rates. Management took advantage of the lower stock price earlier in the year, repurchasing $950mm of stock in the first half. Investors responded favorably to growing evidence that IQVIA's AI-enabled offerings are supporting client demand and productivity, reinforcing confidence in the company's long-term growth outlook.

Top detractor

DSV was a detractor during the quarter. Shares of the Danish freight forwarding and logistics company declined following a quarterly earnings report that highlighted operational challenges within its Road division. Network and IT issues in several European markets weighed on profitability and investor sentiment, overshadowing stronger results in the company's Air & Sea and Contract Logistics businesses. Management remains focused on integrating its 2025 acquisition of DB Schenker and responded quickly to the Road division challenges by appointing an experienced DSV executive to lead the business. Management has confirmed that service levels have already improved significantly. Despite near-term execution issues, we remain confident in the investment case of the Schenker acquisition and DSV's ability to integrate the two businesses. This combination should lead to meaningful cost synergies and profitability improvement over time.

Portfolio Activity

New purchases

Amrize is a leading producer of building materials and construction solutions, established following Holcim's spin-off of its North American operations in June '25. Amrize holds strong market positions—it is the largest cement producer, the second-largest commercial roofing products manufacturer and a top-five aggregates producer in the U.S. and Canada. The company benefits from meaningful pricing power due to its scale, advantaged regional footprint and tight supply dynamics. We also see long-term potential in the Building Envelope segment, which has been built up through acquisitions over the last five years. We believe there is a path to closing a substantial portion of the margin gap to roofing peers. In our view, Amrize is a strong business that is flying under the radar of U.S. investors. This created the opportunity to invest alongside a proven CEO that is focused on unlocking substantial value.

LVMH (Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessy) is the world's largest luxury goods company with a portfolio of 75 brands, including prestigious houses Louis Vuitton and Dior. In our view, the company is well diversified by product category and region, which has allowed LVMH to strategically tier pricing and cater to a wide range of customers. Additionally, we like that the company operates a differentiated model with scarcity coming from limited editions, collaborations and capsule collections with small run times, which has enabled LVMH to grow its market share and deliver attractive organic growth and returns through cycles. Recently, the luxury goods market has come under pressure as a result of U.S. demand moderating, European stagnation and a difficult Chinese macro backdrop. We expect the industry to recover to historical levels and believe LVMH can further benefit from self-help initiatives in the form of product innovation and improved cost discipline. This provided the rare opportunity to purchase shares in LVMH at a discounted valuation to its peers and the company's own trading history.

Willis Towers Watson (WTW) is a leading insurance broker and HR services firm. It operates in a capital-light industry with high returns on equity and attractive free cash flow generation. WTW has consistently generated mid-single digit organic revenue growth and delivered significant margin expansion since present management took over. Recently, WTW announced updated targets for even higher margins enabled by efficiency initiatives and AI benefits that further narrow the gap to other leading brokers. We believe the shares are undervalued on both an absolute basis and relative to the multiples at which comparable companies trade today.

New purchases

Meta Platforms is a U.S.-headquartered technology company whose Family of Apps (including Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp) reaches 3.6 billion daily active users. Growth and returns in Meta's core businesses remain exceptional but investors have grown concerned by the company's large investment in AI. We are confident that the company can monetize AI compute through a combination of core business improvement, new AI businesses and potentially 3rd party compute rental. We believe the Family of Apps business is already benefitting from improved recommendation and ad-matching systems. Meta is also off to a strong start with its new personal AI assistant, Muse. With shares trading near their lowest multiple outside the 2022 period, we invested at a meaningful discount to our estimate of intrinsic value.

Sugi Holdings is one of Japan's largest drugstore chains and is uniquely positioned through its nationwide network of pharmacy-equipped stores, which provide a stable and growing healthcare-focused revenue base. The company continues to benefit from favorable demographic trends, ongoing consolidation in Japan's drugstore and dispensing

pharmacy markets, and a strong track record of disciplined M&A. Under founder-led management, Sugi has also emerged as a leader in digital initiatives and AI adoption, using technology to improve efficiency, margins, and customer engagement. We believe the market is overlooking the company's long-term growth opportunities, including further industry consolidation, strategic partnerships, creating an attractive risk-reward profile at current valuation levels.
